references.text: The clay pot in which the sin offering was boiled must be broken. The same principle applies: clay pots that have come into contact with holy or unclean things must be destroyed.
If something unclean falls into a clay pot, it becomes unclean, and the pot must be broken. A parallel law concerning clay pots that become unclean.
Wooden objects that become unclean must be placed in water. The same cleansing method applies to wooden vessels as in Leviticus 15:12.
Any bed or object on which a person with a discharge sits becomes unclean. Context for how discharges make objects unclean.
Open containers without lids become unclean. Related purity laws concerning vessels and objects.
Anything that can withstand fire must be purified by fire, and anything that cannot withstand fire must be purified by water. Different cleansing methods for different materials.
